B ties the diagnosis to the Room 5 incident more closely and is clearer about what to leave alone, but its first fix is alerting rather than a visual change. A follows the requested fix order more closely, but it says little about what to keep. Neither answer clearly makes the in-range state quieter. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B sees the core problem most clearly. In-range and out-of-range rooms look the same, and the alert word is styled more quietly than the labels next to it. B's first fix makes out-of-range rooms stand out through a status band, a bold status word with duration, the target range and sorting, so it matches the rubric's priority. A's look at alert duration and notifications is useful, but it puts alerting ahead of the visual fix. Neither answer clearly proposes making in-range cards quieter or says much about what to keep.
